bull.b: Rapid revenue growth alongside expansion in large enterprise customers indicates broadening adoption across Cloudflare’s platform. A growing enterprise base can improve recurring revenue durability, increase cross-selling opportunities, and strengthen the company’s competitive position over the next several quarters.

A 120% dollar-based net retention rate shows existing customers are expanding their spending rather than merely renewing. This land-and-expand model supports predictable subscription growth, raises customer lifetime value, and provides a durable foundation for continued revenue compounding.

Strong free cash flow demonstrates that Cloudflare’s subscription and usage-based model is converting growth into real liquidity despite GAAP losses. A substantial cash balance also supports infrastructure investment, product development, and strategic flexibility without relying solely on external financing.

bear.b: Persistent GAAP losses show that Cloudflare has not yet established durable bottom-line profitability, even as revenue scales. Continued losses can constrain internal capital formation, increase dependence on non-GAAP adjustments, and make execution on the path to sustainable earnings especially important.

Leverage is high relative to the company’s current profitability profile and reduces financial flexibility if growth slows or funding conditions tighten. Debt obligations can absorb cash that could otherwise support investment, while negative returns on equity indicate that borrowed capital is not yet producing durable shareholder returns.

The year-over-year gross margin decline indicates that incremental growth is currently carrying a heavier network-cost burden. If this pressure persists, it could limit operating leverage, reduce the cash contribution from each dollar of revenue, and make future profitability improvement more difficult.
